title: Time Magazine Provides Special Edition Pages to AI Crawlers: Embedded Advertisements in Markdown Format That Humans Can't See
excerpt: The magazine Time was found to provide completely different access versions for human readers and AI crawlers, sparking widespread attention in the digital publ
content_html:
The magazine Time was found to provide completely different access versions for human readers and AI crawlers, sparking widespread attention in the digital publishing industry. Developer Vincent Schmalbach discovered this by changing the User-Agent during testing. When accessed through a regular browser, the website returned a standard HTML page of about 303KB, while switching the access identity to ClaudeBot or PerplexityBot resulted in only a 13KB Markdown format content, with the response header explicitly set to text/markdown. This design means that Time is customizing easily parseable text content for AI systems, rather than letting crawlers extract information from complex web pages on their own.

More intriguingly, these Markdown pages designed for AI crawlers also include targeted advertisements provided by the AI advertising technology company Mobian. To make it easier for generative AI to read advertiser information, the pages embed sponsored content in a Q&A format. These advertisements are clearly marked as sponsored, but they do not appear at all when human readers access the standard page. In other words, when users search for Time magazine content through AI tools like ChatGPT or Perplexity, the AI might inadvertently "read out" brand advertisements in its response, without the user being aware of it.

New Strategies for Publishers to Gain Control in the AI Era

This strategy reveals a new approach for publishers in monetizing in the AI era. Under traditional models, publishers earned revenue through display ads and subscriptions, but when AI crawlers scraped content and directly returned summaries, users no longer visited the original webpages, leading to loss of traffic and advertising revenue. By providing specialized pages for AI crawlers and embedding advertisements, Time attempts to retain commercial monetization within AI search results, directly embedding brand information into AI-generated responses.

This practice has also sparked discussions about transparency and ethical boundaries. Whether AI search engines should indicate in their answers that the content includes sponsored information, and whether users have the right to know which parts of an AI response are influenced by advertisements, remains unclear. As more publishers follow this model, the issue of ad transparency in the AI search ecosystem will become an unavoidable topic for the industry. Time's attempt may just be the beginning of the struggle between publishers and AI platforms.

content_html_zh:
《时代》杂志被发现为人类读者和人工智能爬虫提供了完全不同的访问版本，引发了数字出版行业的广泛关注。 开发人员 Vincent Schmalbach 通过在测试期间更改用户代理发现了这一点。 通过普通浏览器访问时，该网站返回了约303KB的标准HTML页面，而切换访问身份为ClaudeBot或PerplexityBot则仅得到13KB的Markdown格式内容，响应头显式设置为text/markdown。 这种设计意味着时代正在为人工智能系统定制易于解析的文本内容，而不是让爬虫自行从复杂的网页中提取信息。

更有趣的是，这些为AI爬虫设计的Markdown页面还包含AI广告技术公司Mobian提供的定向广告。 为了使生成式人工智能更容易读取广告商信息，这些页面以问答形式嵌入了赞助内容。 这些广告被明确标记为赞助广告，但当人类读者访问标准页面时，它们根本不会出现。 换句话说，当用户通过 ChatGPT 或 Perplexity 等人工智能工具搜索《时代》杂志内容时，人工智能可能会在用户不知情的情况下无意中“读出”品牌广告。

出版商在人工智能时代获得控制权的新策略

这一策略为出版商在人工智能时代创收提供了一种新方法。 传统模式下，发布商通过展示广告和订阅获得收入，但当人工智能爬虫抓取内容并直接返回摘要时，用户不再访问原始网页，导致流量和广告收入损失。 通过为人工智能爬虫提供专门的页面并嵌入广告，时代试图在人工智能搜索结果中保留商业货币化，直接将品牌信息嵌入人工智能生成的响应中。

这种做法还引发了有关透明度和道德界限的讨论。 人工智能搜索引擎是否应在其答案中表明内容包含赞助信息，以及用户是否有权知道人工智能响应的哪些部分受到广告的影响，目前尚不清楚。 随着越来越多的出版商效仿这一模式，人工智能搜索生态系统中的广告透明度问题将成为业界不可避免的话题​​。 Time的尝试或许只是出版商与AI平台斗争的开始。
